Azure Mastery is free to download, with a starter set of questions for every supported exam. You can buy each full question bank with a one-time in-app purchase. Core study features need no subscription, and you can start without an account. Which Microsoft certifications does Azure Mastery cover? Azure Mastery covers 30 Microsoft certification exams: AZ-900, AZ-104, AZ-305, AZ-400, AZ-700, AI-901, AI-103, AI-200, AI-300, AI-500, AB-100, AB-410, AB-620, AB-650, AB-731, AB-900, DP-900, DP-300, DP-700, DP-750, DP-800, SC-900, SC-100, SC-200, SC-300, SC-500, PL-300, PL-900, GH-900, and GH-300. The app spans Azure infrastructure, AI engineering, data, security and compliance, Microsoft 365 Copilot administration, AI transformation leadership, SQL AI development, agentic AI architecture, multi-agent AI engineering, and Power BI roles. How does the Exam IQ score work? Exam IQ uses a CoreML model on your device to estimate your exam-day score and a confidence range. It considers your accuracy in each domain, question coverage, mastery, consistency, and how recently you practised. The range narrows as you answer more questions. Your answers stay on your device. More questions about the app What is Ask Aura? Ask Aura Preview is the private Pro study companion in Azure Mastery 2.0. It starts with reviewed material for your current exam, shows source cards behind its answers, can quiz you, turn Exam IQ priorities into a focused study session, and bring saved takeaways back when they are due. Saved conversations stay on your device, and temporary chats are not saved. Does Azure Mastery work offline? Yes. Questions, Exam IQ score prediction, adaptive study plans, written Answer Coach guidance, and Ask Aura's bundled study material work offline. Optional Microsoft Learn lookups need a connection and stay off until you enable them. If you choose to sync, it uses your private iCloud account. Azure Mastery has no server for your study data and does not track how you use the app. Does Azure Mastery support iPad and Apple Watch? Yes. Azure Mastery is a native SwiftUI app for iPhone and iPad, with Stage Manager support and layouts for larger iPad screens. The Apple Watch companion shows your daily streak and XP. Live Activities show your study timer on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island. How is Azure Mastery different from other Microsoft exam prep apps? Azure Mastery helps you know when you're ready and what to practise next. It compares your predicted score with Microsoft's pass threshold and estimates your ability in each exam domain, so you can see which areas need work. Spaced repetition helps you revisit topics you're starting to forget. The machine learning runs on your device without tracking your activity. What kinds of practice questions are included? The app includes 12,600+ practice questions across 30 Microsoft exams. Azure Mastery uses nine interactive, exam-style formats including multiple choice, multi-select, drag-and-drop ordering, hotspot, and case studies; the live exam's exact interface and item mix are controlled by Microsoft and may differ. Every question includes the correct reasoning and an explanation, with option-by-option rationale where available. Choose whether explanations appear after each question or at the end of a practice test, then jump straight to missed answers; Answer Coach keeps its session notes ready when you revisit. Who makes Azure Mastery? Azure Mastery is published by Moonbeam Alpha Ltd, an independent iOS app studio focused on certification preparation. The app is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft. entries.text: About About Azure Mastery Who makes Azure Mastery, what the app does, and how it's built. Who makes it Who makes Azure Mastery Azure Mastery is published by Moonbeam Alpha Ltd , an independent iOS app studio focused on certification preparation. The app is designed, built, and maintained by its developer. Moonbeam Alpha Ltd is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Microsoft Corporation. Microsoft, Azure, and the certification names referenced throughout this site are trademarks of Microsoft Corporation, used here only to describe which exams the app covers. What it is What Azure Mastery is Azure Mastery is a native SwiftUI exam-prep app for iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch, built for Microsoft certification exams across Azure, AI, Data, Security, Power Platform, and GitHub. It runs on iOS 18 and iPadOS 18 or later, with an Apple Watch companion for streaks and daily progress. Exam IQ, the adaptive study plan, Answer Coach and knowledge-decay tracking work together, all on your device: Exam IQ predicts your likely exam score, with a confidence range that narrows as you practise. The adaptive study plan reorders what to revise next based on your actual answers. Answer Coach turns a missed question into a private explanation, grounded in the app's own written rationales. Knowledge-decay tracking flags topics fading from memory before they cost you marks on exam day. The app is free to download, and one-time in-app purchases unlock full per-exam question banks. Core study features need no subscription and no account. The question bank, Exam IQ, the adaptive study plan and Answer Coach's explanations all work offline, with no study-data server and no behavioural tracking. Why it exists Why Azure Mastery exists Most exam-prep apps optimise for volume: thousands of questions, each with barely more than a correct answer marked. Azure Mastery works from a different premise. You learn faster from understanding why an option is right or wrong than from memorising an answer key. Every question carries an explanation, and where an option-by-option rationale exists, it covers the wrong answers as well as the right one. Get a question wrong, and you walk away with a study session, not just a red mark. How it's built How it's built Every practice question follows Microsoft's published skills outline for its exam. Automated checks run whenever a bank changes, and scheduled reviews look for content that's gone stale — see how we write and verify questions . Score prediction and the adaptive study plan run on a CoreML model that reads your practice history on your device, with no server involved — see how Exam IQ works . Independence & privacy Independence and privacy Azure Mastery is an independent study app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Microsoft Corporation, and it is not an official Microsoft product. Microsoft, Azure, and the certification names used throughout this site and the app are trademarks of Microsoft Corporation, used here only to describe which exams the app covers. The app needs as little of your data as possible. The Privacy Policy explains what runs on your device, what can sync through your private iCloud account, and what Moonbeam Alpha Ltd collects. Contact Contact For help with the app or a practice question, visit the Support page . It has contact details and answers to common questions.

entries.text: Privacy Policy Azure Mastery Effective Date: September 23, 2026 Azure Mastery ("the App") is developed and maintained by Azure Mastery ("we", "us", or "our"). This Privacy Policy describes how we handle your information when you use the App. Our Core Commitment Azure Mastery is designed with privacy at its foundation. We do not sell your data, run advertising, or operate an analytics service. Your study progress, preferences, and performance data stay on your device and, if you enable sync, in your private iCloud account. Ask Aura's optional connections are described below. Information We Do NOT Collect Personal identification (email, phone number, date of birth, address) Device identifiers or advertising IDs (IDFA) Location data Photos, camera, contacts, or calendar data Browsing or search history Analytics, telemetry, or usage tracking Crash reports sent to third parties The App contains no third-party analytics SDKs, advertising frameworks, or tracking libraries. Information Stored on Your Device The App stores the following data locally on your device to provide its core functionality: Study Progress Questions attempted, correct answers, and response times Practice test scores and completion dates Mastery levels, streaks, and XP totals Study session history and daily activity Achievement records Bookmarked questions Preferences and Settings Appearance mode (light, dark, or system) Text size preferences Notification settings (reminders, streak protection, exam countdown) Goal exams, certification paths, and exam target dates Experience level selection Profile Display name and initials (optional, user-provided) All of this data is stored using Apple's SwiftData framework and UserDefaults on your device. iCloud Sync The App offers an optional iCloud sync feature, controlled by a toggle in Settings. When enabled: Your study progress and preferences sync to your private iCloud account via Apple CloudKit. This data is stored in your personal iCloud container and is not accessible to us or any third party. Syncing allows you to access your progress across your Apple devices. You can disable iCloud sync at any time in the App's Settings. iCloud data is governed by Apple's Privacy Policy . In-App Purchases The App offers premium subscriptions (monthly, annual) and a lifetime access option, as well as individual exam pack purchases. All transactions are processed entirely by Apple through StoreKit. We do not collect or have access to your payment information, Apple ID, or billing details. In-app purchase data is governed by Apple's Privacy Policy . On-Device Intelligence The App includes machine learning features that predict exam readiness and forecast scores. These models: Run entirely on your device using Apple's CoreML framework. Do not send any data to external servers for processing. Use only your locally stored study metrics as input. Ask Aura's initial preview uses reviewed study material and deterministic local study routes. Generative coaching is not enabled in this build. On supported iOS 27 devices, optional speech transcription uses an on-device model to create an editable draft; it does not generate Ask Aura answers. Ask Aura Preview Ask Aura begins with reviewed material bundled with the App, including study guides, terminology, question explanations, and on-device Exam IQ insights. Saved Ask Aura conversations stay on the device where they were created and are excluded from app cloud sync and backups. Temporary chats are not saved. The App does not send your conversations, answers, or study progress to Azure Mastery or Moonbeam Alpha servers. Microsoft Learn lookups This optional connection is off by default. If you enable it, Ask Aura may request public Microsoft documentation using a public topic name or documentation address. Microsoft does not receive your full message, answer history, or study progress from this feature. The request requires an internet connection and is governed by Microsoft's Privacy Statement . Apple Private Cloud Compute Private Cloud Compute explanations are not enabled in the initial Ask Aura preview build. If a future build enables this route, it will remain optional and off until you choose to enable it. When enabled and used, relevant messages and selected study excerpts may be sent to Apple for a more complex explanation. Availability and usage limits are controlled by Apple and processing is governed by Apple's Privacy Policy . Voice input On supported iOS 27 devices, you can use on-device dictation in Ask Aura. Microphone audio is used only while dictation is active. Azure Mastery does not save that audio, include it with the message, or send the resulting editable draft until you choose to send it. Notifications The App can send local notifications for daily study reminders, streak protection, and exam countdown alerts. These are scheduled locally on your device and do not involve any external push notification service. You control which notifications are enabled in the App's Settings, and you can revoke notification permission at any time through iOS Settings. Widgets and Apple Watch The App provides home screen widgets and an Apple Watch companion app. These extensions access a limited subset of your study data (readiness score, streak, daily progress, XP) through Apple's secure App Groups mechanism. This data never leaves your device. Support Contact If you choose to report a question issue, the App opens your device's native Mail app with a pre-filled email to support@moonbeamalpha.atlassian.net. The email is sent through your own email account — we only receive what you choose to send. We do not automatically collect your email address. Content Updates The App may check for content updates (new questions or exam material) from a hosted manifest file. This check: Does not transmit any personal data or device information. Only downloads a small metadata file to determine if new content is available. Can be performed over standard HTTPS. Children's Privacy The App does not knowingly collect information from children under 13. The App is an educational study tool and does not contain user accounts, social features, or age-gated content. External Services The App uses Apple's platform frameworks and services, including SwiftUI, SwiftData, StoreKit, CoreML, CloudKit, WidgetKit, and WatchConnectivity. Ask Aura can also make the optional Microsoft Learn request described above. We do not include third-party advertising, analytics, or tracking SDKs. Data Retention and Deletion All data is stored locally on your device. You can delete all App data at any time by: Deleting the App from your device (removes all local data). Disabling iCloud sync and removing the App's iCloud data through Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Manage Storage on your device. We do not operate a server that retains your study data or Ask Aura conversations. External services may process the limited data described in the optional-connections sections under their own privacy terms. Changes to This Policy We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Changes will be reflected by updating the "Effective Date" at the top of this document. Continued use of the App after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy. Contact Us If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, contact us at: support@moonbeamalpha.atlassian.net Apple App Store Privacy Details Data Not Collected : The App does not collect any data. Data Not Linked to You : No data is linked to your identity. Data Not Used to Track You : The App does not track you across other companies' apps or websites.

AB-100 is the Microsoft Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect credential — the senior-architect exam for designing, deploying, and governing agentic-first business solutions across the full Microsoft AI stack: Copilot Studio , Microsoft Foundry , Microsoft 365 Copilot , Dynamics 365 Copilot , and Power Platform AI . It covers: Plan AI-powered business solutions — ROI analysis, multi-agent strategy Design agents and orchestration — task, autonomous, and prompt-and-response agents, MCP extensibility, Foundry Tools Deploy with full ALM, telemetry, responsible AI, and security AB-100 tests architecture decisions across several Microsoft platforms. You'll: Analyse business requirements and choose whether to build or buy an agent solution Design multi-agent systems with Agent2Agent (A2A) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) Work across Microsoft 365 Copilot for Sales and Service and Dynamics 365 AI Manage lifecycle, governance, and audit trails for agents and models Scenarios ask you to choose a component, deployment slot, or control that fits the wider business system. Microsoft's current AB-100 skills are measured as of 22 July 2026 . Every question in Azure Mastery's AB-100 bank is mapped to the current outline — including the new MCP extensibility, Computer Use, agent feed, and DSPM-for-AI topics. Read the official outline at learn.microsoft.com . Questions 40–60 questions, mixed formats Duration 100 minutes (120 min seat) Pass score 700 / 1000 Cost USD $165 (≈ £128 UK) Validity Renew annually Format Online or test centre Skills measured · 22 July 2026 AB-100 exam objectives Three domains from Microsoft's current outline, skills measured as of 22 July 2026 . Every domain below lists Microsoft's own skill groups verbatim from the official study guide , so you always know which domain you're being tested on and where your weak spots cluster. AI & agent skill map Plan AI-powered business solutions Published weight 25–30% 124 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Plan topics Analyze requirements for AI-powered business solutions Design overall AI strategy for business solutions Evaluate the costs and benefits of an AI-powered business solution Covers assessing where agents genuinely help, checking grounding-data quality, and sequencing adoption with the Cloud Adoption Framework's AI track. The ROI and total-cost-of-ownership case gets skipped in favour of jumping straight to a build-versus-buy answer without the numbers. Practise arguing when a model router beats a single model on cost versus capability before picking either. Design AI-powered business solutions Published weight 25–30% 131 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Design topics Design AI and agents for business solutions Design extensibility of AI solutions Orchestrate configuration for prebuilt agents and apps Spans the most surfaces: task, autonomous, and prompt-and-response agents, plus Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility choices. Candidates default to a custom Foundry build when a declarative Microsoft 365 Copilot extension already covers the requirement. Match Model Context Protocol, Computer Use, or a Copilot Studio topic to the exact extensibility need described. Deploy AI-powered business solutions Published weight 40–45% 188 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Deploy topics Analyze, monitor, and tune AI-powered business solutions Manage the testing of AI-powered business solutions Design the ALM process for AI-powered business solutions Design responsible AI, security, governance, risk management, and compliance The heaviest domain: telemetry interpretation, validation criteria, and lifecycle management across Copilot Studio, Foundry, and custom models. Governance is the biggest theme here, and candidates underweight prompt-manipulation mitigations and data-residency controls. Trace one agent's audit trail and grounding-data access controls before assuming security means model safety alone. Common traps Where AB-100 candidates slip Five recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AB-100 candidates, grounded in the current skills outline. The right answer matches the stated constraint Candidates pick a design that's correct for a different constraint than the one the scenario actually states. Cost, residency, governance, and time-to-market are the four constraints that repeatedly decide the correct answer here. Read the stem for its stated constraint first, then evaluate every option only against that one requirement. Smallest sufficient capability beats the most powerful one Candidates reach for the most powerful platform option when the scenario's requirements are satisfied by a lighter one. A declarative extension or prebuilt feature beats a custom build whenever it already satisfies the stated requirement. Ask whether the scenario actually demands the heavier option's extra capability before choosing it. Know which platform owns a capability by default Candidates can't say which platform is the intended surface when several technically overlap on the same capability. Several platforms can technically do the same job, but the exam rewards naming the one Microsoft intends for it. Decide whether the scenario is extending an existing Copilot experience or building a new agent from scratch. Responsible AI requirements are design constraints, not an afterthought Candidates treat responsible AI as a separate checklist item instead of applying the specific safety, privacy, transparency, or oversight requirement in the scenario. A named Responsible AI requirement can rule out an otherwise viable design, but it is not an automatic tie-breaker when the scenario does not call for that control. Look for an impact assessment, content-safety classifier, audit trail, or refusal pattern as the tie-breaking detail. The scenario paragraph carries the answer Candidates miss a compliance requirement or staffing limit buried in the setup that decides the correct design. A compliance requirement or staffing limit stated once in the setup often isn't repeated anywhere in the question itself. Read the full business scenario once before touching any option, including the setup paragraph and the question line. 10-week study plan Suggested AB-100 study plan Start with business planning, then design agents and practise deployment. Use this ten-week route at your own pace, with time for testing, governance and review. Requirements and grounding Identify automation, analytics and decision-support use cases. Check grounding data for accuracy, relevance and timeliness. Organise business data for AI consumption. AI strategy Review the Cloud Adoption Framework AI guidance. Compare Copilot, Copilot Studio and Foundry for multi-agent solutions. Plan build, buy or extend choices, prompt guidelines and an AI centre of excellence. Value and investment Estimate total cost of ownership. Compare the ROI of building, buying and extending. Explore AI scenarios across Dynamics 365 apps. Agent design Compare task, autonomous and conversational agents. Design Copilot customisations for Dynamics 365 customer experience and service. Use Foundry Tools and Copilot Studio topics with fallback. Extensibility Explore custom models in Foundry and agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Review MCP extensions and Computer Use. Design agent reasoning, behaviour and voice interactions. Prebuilt agents Explore agents for Dynamics 365 finance, supply chain and customer service. Compare Microsoft 365 Copilot for Sales and Service scenarios. Review Power Platform AI Hub and model routing. Monitoring and tuning Use agent-monitoring tools and interpret telemetry. Turn user feedback and backlog findings into improvements. Review model-performance metrics. Testing Define an agent test strategy and success metrics. Set validation criteria for custom AI models. Test prompts and end-to-end scenarios across Dynamics 365 apps. Deployment and governance Plan ALM for data, agents, models and Dynamics 365 AI. Review security, access controls and prompt-manipulation mitigations. Check responsible AI, data residency and audit trails. Review and rehearse Use Focus Weak Spots to revisit weaker domains. Complete two timed, 100-minute Exam Simulator sessions. Review mistakes and use the results to guide further study.

Azure Mastery uses on-device AI to predict your readiness score across all three AB-410 domains, build a personalised study plan from your weak spots, and surface topics you're forgetting. Core study stays on-device and works offline; optional sync uses your private iCloud account. The exam What is the AB-410 exam? AB-410 is the Microsoft Intelligent Applications Builder credential — the role-based exam for makers who build AI-powered business solutions in Microsoft Power Platform using Copilot, natural-language prompts and low-code tools. It covers: Laying the foundation — solution design, environments, ALM and the Dataverse data model Creating the applications — model-driven and canvas apps, including generative pages built from a written description Building the logic and automation behind them — cloud flows, AI Hub prompts and AI Builder models, business rules and process flows It is the successor route for makers who previously targeted PL-200 — Microsoft replaced the PL-200T00 course with AB-410T00. AB-410 tests practical Power Platform development: choosing the right component (model-driven app, canvas app, cloud flow, Power Pages site, or agent), modelling data in Dataverse, and building the logic behind it. Constraints matter: must a rule fire on every write, block a save, or call an outside service? Practise Power Fx, prompt columns, and the differences between calculated, rollup, and formula columns. Microsoft's AB-410 study guide was last updated on 15 May 2026 . Every question in Azure Mastery's AB-410 bank is mapped to that current three-domain outline and was reviewed against it in August 2026. Read the official Microsoft study guide . Questions Typically 40–60 Duration 100 minutes (120 min seat) Pass score 700 / 1000 Cost USD $165 typical; varies by region Validity Renew annually (Associate) Format Proctored; interactive components may appear Skills measured · 15 May 2026 AB-410 exam objectives Three domains, with weights set by Microsoft's 15 May 2026 update. The skill groups under each domain below are Microsoft's own wording, lifted verbatim from the official study guide , so you can pinpoint exactly where a weak spot belongs. AI & agent skill map Create a foundation for intelligent applications Published weight 25–30% 123 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Foundation topics Design Microsoft Power Platform Solutions by Using AI-Enabled Tools Build Data Models Tests whether you can match a stated requirement to a component and an environment before writing a formula. Candidates skip straight to app design and get the Dataverse data model wrong, which every later domain inherits. Learn prompt columns and row summaries by exactly what they ground an answer against. Create intelligent applications Published weight 25–30% 138 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Apps topics Create Model-Driven Apps Create Canvas Apps Recognising whether a scenario needs a model-driven app or a canvas app is the real test before any configuration question. Generative pages get treated as decoration rather than a real alternative to a hand-built form or view. Learn named formulas separately from ordinary variables; the exam distinguishes them by how each one updates. Build business application logic and automation Published weight 40–45% 183 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Logic topics Create Cloud Flows Create Prompts and Models in AI Hub Implement Business and Process Logic A business rule, a cloud flow, or an AI Hub prompt each suit a different piece of logic, and picking the right one is the point. A cloud flow gets reached for by default, even when a save-blocking requirement actually calls for a business rule. Learn which of calculated, rollup, and formula columns updates on which schedule before exam day, not during it. Common traps Where AB-410 candidates slip Four recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AB-410 candidates, grounded in the current study guide. A business rule, a cloud flow, and a plug-in are not interchangeable AB-410 stems describe logic that must run on every write, and candidates reach for a cloud flow out of habit. The exam is testing whether you know a business rule fires synchronously and can block a save, while a cloud flow runs after the fact. Pick a business rule whenever the requirement says the record must never be saved invalid. Calculated, rollup, and formula columns update on different schedules All three column types look identical on a form, which is exactly why AB-410 tests the difference between them. The exam is testing whether you know calculated runs on retrieve, rollup runs on a schedule, and formula runs Power Fx on read. Rule out the rollup column immediately whenever the scenario needs a value that's always current, not scheduled. A named formula is not the same thing as a global variable Canvas-app questions test whether you reach for App.OnStart out of habit instead of a named formula. A variable set in OnStart only holds a value if OnStart actually ran, a condition that's easy to overlook. Use a named formula wherever a value should always be correct, since it recalculates automatically when inputs change. Model-driven, canvas, and Power Pages solve different distribution problems A scenario naming an audience with no Dataverse licence or tenant identity is describing Power Pages, not a canvas app. Matching many related tables and generated navigation to model-driven, not canvas, is exactly what's being scored. Read who the audience is and whether they hold a Dataverse licence before choosing between the three options. 6-week study plan Suggested AB-410 study plan Build from requirements and Dataverse to apps and automation. Follow this six-week route, adjusting the pace to your Power Platform experience. Plan the solution Match requirements to components and built-in agents. Choose extensibility options and environment types. Define a solution and ALM strategy. Model the data Create Dataverse tables, columns and relationships. Configure prompt columns and row summaries. Build views and forms; apply Dataverse security. Compose intelligent apps Create model-driven forms and views. Build generative pages from written descriptions. Configure the site map, charts and dashboards. Build canvas apps Connect data sources and improve accessibility and performance. Use components, named formulas, functions, variables and collections. Handle errors and test with Monitor. Automate business logic Build cloud flows with triggers, connectors, approvals and branching. Use AI Hub prompts and AI Builder models. Configure business rules, process flows and calculated, rollup or formula columns. Review and rehearse Use Focus Weak Spots to revisit weaker topics. Complete two timed, 120-minute Exam Simulator sessions. Review mistakes before deciding what to study next.

Core study stays on-device and works offline; optional sync uses your private iCloud account. The exam What is the AB-620 exam? AB-620 is the Microsoft AI Agent Builder credential — the role-based exam for designing and building integrated AI agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio . AB-620 covers planning agent solutions, building and integrating agents in Copilot Studio (topics, generative answers, tools, MCP integrations, channels), and testing / managing agents in production (analytics, deployment lifecycle, governance). AB-620 is hands-on and Copilot-Studio-aware . It covers: Plan and configure agent solutions — use cases, environments, conversational design, integrations Integrate and extend agents in Copilot Studio — trigger-phrase topics, generative orchestration, SharePoint and Dataverse knowledge sources, custom plugins via Power Platform connectors and MCP Test and manage agents — test pane, analytics, channels, lifecycle, governance, security Expect scenario questions that show you a Copilot Studio topic configuration or generative-answer setup and ask what to change. Microsoft last updated the AB-620 study guide on 21 April 2026 . Every question in Azure Mastery's AB-620 bank is mapped to the current outline. Read the official Microsoft study guide . Questions 40–60 questions, mixed formats Duration 100 minutes (120 min seat) Pass score 700 / 1000 Cost USD $165 (≈ £128 UK) Validity Renew annually (Associate) Format Online or test centre Study guide updated · 21 April 2026 AB-620 exam objectives Three domains from Microsoft's current outline. Every domain below lists Microsoft's own skill groups verbatim from the official study guide , so you always know which domain you're being tested on and where your weak spots cluster. AI & agent skill map Plan and configure agent solutions Published weight 30–35% 135 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Plan topics Plan an Agent Solution Create and Monitor Agent Flows in Copilot Studio Configure Topics Covers audience, identity, channel, and governance choices made before any conversation logic gets built. The identity-model decision gets skipped: a Teams-only agent and a public website agent need different auth models. Learn how a topic calls a flow, a tool, or a custom-prompt node — that's the exam's real question shape. Integrate and extend agents in Copilot Studio Published weight 40–45% 170 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Integrate topics Connect to Enterprise Knowledge Sources Add Tools to Agents Configure Multi-Agent Collaboration from Copilot Studio Integrate Agents with Azure The largest domain: grounding sources, connector types, and multi-agent delegation to Foundry, Copilot Studio, or Fabric agents. Candidates can't tell a custom connector, an MCP tool, and computer-use automation apart for a given integration. Practise wiring Azure AI Search or the Foundry model catalogue directly into a topic's generative-answer setup. Test and manage agents Published weight 20–25% 82 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Manage topics Evaluate Agent Performance Implement Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) for Agents in Copilot Studio Smallest domain but operational: building a test set, choosing an evaluation method, then packaging the agent for release. Environment variables and connection references are what let a pipeline move an agent without manual copying — easy to forget. Trace one agent through a full Power Platform pipeline from dev to production before exam day. Common traps Where AB-620 candidates slip Five recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AB-620 candidates, grounded in the current skills outline. Connector vs. MCP tool vs. agent flow Candidates can't tell a connector, an MCP tool, and an agent flow apart when a scenario needs one of the three. A stable API points to a connector, a dynamically discovered schema points to an MCP tool, and multi-step orchestration points to an agent flow. Look for the named constraint in the scenario — stability, discovery, or approvals — it picks one of the three for you. Topics handle conversation, flows handle the backend Candidates treat an agent flow as just a topic with extra steps, missing which layer owns a piece of logic. A topic decides what the agent says next; an agent flow decides what happens in the systems behind it. Ask whether the described behaviour is what the agent says or what happens behind the scenes before answering. A2A protocol vs. an embedded sub-agent Candidates read "integrating a Foundry agent" without noticing whether it's a separate A2A agent or an embedded sub-agent. A child agent receives the parent agent's context and uses its own tools and knowledge. A connected A2A agent remains a separately managed agent, with context hand-off controlled by the connection. Check the endpoint, context setting, and authentication requirements instead of assuming permissions are inherited. Groundedness rules aren't optional Candidates assume a correct-sounding answer is enough, but Copilot Studio can withhold a knowledge-source response when ungrounded responses are disabled and the answer lacks an in-text citation. Groundedness evaluation checks whether an answer is supported by the supplied context; citation behaviour is a separate product setting and response requirement. For a "confidently wrong agent" scenario, inspect the knowledge source, orchestration, citation, and ungrounded-response settings before blaming the model. Identity choice depends on audience, not habit Candidates default to one identity model out of habit instead of matching it to who or what is calling the agent. User-delegated tokens, service principals, and managed identities each map to a different kind of caller. Ask whether a known Entra user or an unauthenticated external caller is making the request before choosing an identity model. 6-week study plan Suggested AB-620 study plan Plan an agent, build its conversations and integrations, then test and manage it. Use this six-week route at a pace that suits your Copilot Studio experience. Plan the agent Identify use cases and compare custom agents with templates. Plan Dataverse environments. Choose channels such as Teams, Microsoft 365, web or voice. Design conversations Define entry points and fallback responses. Plan escalation to a person. Review DLP, sharing and environment security roles. Build topics and orchestration Create topics and trigger phrases. Use conversation nodes, variables and branching. Explore generative orchestration for dynamic responses. Connect knowledge and tools Add knowledge from SharePoint, Dataverse, websites, files or Azure AI Search. Connect Power Automate, MCP and AI Builder tools. Configure Microsoft Entra and OAuth authentication. Test and manage Inspect variables, trace topics and debug orchestration. Publish to channels and monitor analytics. Manage versions, solutions, environments and governance policies. Review and rehearse Use Focus Weak Spots to revisit weaker topics. Complete two timed, 100-minute Exam Simulator sessions. Review mistakes and repeat the areas that need practice.

Candidates skim this domain as routine admin work, then miss questions on Copilot-specific settings. Learn which licence unlocks which AI surface; Copilot, Agent 365, and Copilot Studio aren't interchangeable. Govern and secure Microsoft 365 tenants and workloads Published weight 40–45% 207 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Govern topics Manage identities in Microsoft Entra Implement and manage authentication and access in Microsoft Entra Secure Microsoft 365 workloads Protect data in Microsoft 365 by using Microsoft Purview Identity, Conditional Access, Defender, and Purview all show up together here, in the domain carrying the largest published weight. A deep identity background can lead you to skim Microsoft Entra Agent ID, assuming it's a footnote on familiar content. Learn Data Loss Prevention and Data Security Posture Management as separate tools that answer different questions. Manage and secure AI services in Microsoft 365 Published weight 35–40% 196 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore AI Services topics Enable and manage Microsoft 365 Copilot Implement and manage agents in Microsoft 365 and Agent 365 Secure and govern agents by using Agent 365 Monitor AI services in Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness, the agent lifecycle through Microsoft Entra Agent ID, and Agent 365 governance are bundled into a single domain. A tenant can hold a Copilot licence and still not be ready for it, a distinction that's easy to miss. Learn the agent registry and Agent 365 policies as governance tools, not agent-building skills. Common traps Where AB-650 candidates slip Five recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AB-650 candidates, grounded in the current study guide. Building an agent and governing one are different job functions AB-650 questions describe an agent that already exists and ask how to license, register, or monitor it. The exam is testing whether you reach for the agent registry or an Agent 365 policy, not Copilot Studio maker skills. Treat any stem about an existing agent as a governance question, never a design question. SC-300 identity depth is not required, but agent identity is exam-specific here Candidates with a deep identity background sometimes skim Microsoft Entra Agent ID, assuming it's a footnote on familiar content. Agent identity carries its own lifecycle and ownership model, quite separate from a human account. Study Microsoft Entra Agent ID directly rather than assuming Conditional Access knowledge covers it. Data Loss Prevention and Data Security Posture Management answer different questions A DLP policy blocks a specific action, while Data Security Posture Management gives visibility into what's already happening. Picking DSPM for visibility into oversharing risk and DLP for blocking an action is exactly what's scored. Ask whether the stem wants enforcement or visibility before choosing between the two controls. Copilot readiness is a distinct configuration step, not a licensing checkbox Assigning a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence doesn't make a tenant ready for it. The exam is testing whether you know oversharing remediation and SharePoint tuning happen before rollout, not the licence itself. Treat unexpected content in Copilot answers as a readiness-work question, not a licensing question. The beta status changes retake eligibility Microsoft allows only one attempt while an exam is in beta. If you do not pass, you can retake it after the exam becomes generally available. The usual 24-hour and 14-day retake waits apply only after the exam is live. Check Microsoft's current beta and retake guidance before booking another attempt. 6-week study plan Suggested AB-650 study plan Move from tenant administration to security and AI services. Practise investigation and attack simulations. Review Purview DLP, sensitivity labels, retention and data security posture. Microsoft 365 Copilot Check tenant readiness and address data oversharing. Review Copilot settings, Search and Cowork. Configure connectors and third-party providers. Agents and AI operations Review the Microsoft Entra Agent ID lifecycle. Explore the agent registry and Agent 365 governance. Monitor AI cost, adoption and health in the Copilot Control System. Review and rehearse Use Focus Weak Spots to revisit difficult distinctions. AB-731 is the Microsoft Certified: AI Transformation Leader credential — the no-code leadership exam for business decision-makers, programme leads, change managers, and AI champions responsible for driving AI adoption across teams and functions. AB-731 validates that you can identify where generative AI adds business value, choose the right Microsoft AI app or service (Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry), and lead an implementation and adoption strategy grounded in responsible AI, licensing trade-offs, and measurable ROI. AB-731 is strategy-first, not hands-on . You aren't expected to write code, build an agent, or configure a tenant. You are expected to: Articulate the difference between generative AI and classical ML Frame token-based cost and ROI Weigh build/buy/extend trade-offs across the Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility framework Set up an AI council and adoption programme Apply Microsoft's responsible-AI principles — fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability Expect scenario questions that put you in a CIO or programme-lead role and ask which Microsoft AI service or governance step fits the business need. AB-731 is the leadership counterpart to the AB-620 builder track and the AB-900 admin track in Microsoft's Copilot and agents family. Learn what RAG buys you at a leadership level; you never need to write the prompt yourself. Identify benefits, capabilities, and opportunities for Microsoft's AI apps and services Published weight 35–40% 131 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Microsoft topics Identify benefits and capabilities of Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Identify benefits and capabilities of Foundry Tools Every business process maps to one exact Microsoft surface, and finding it is the whole exercise. Identify an implementation and adoption strategy for Microsoft's AI apps and services Published weight 20–25% 78 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Strategy topics Align an AI strategy with Microsoft responsible AI policies Plan for AI adoption across the organization Build, buy, and extend trade-offs alongside governance structures and adoption metrics are what's assessed here. This domain gets treated as an afterthought, and marks get lost on the softer governance material. Learn the Copilot Dashboard and adoption metrics as seriously as the two larger technical domains. Common traps Where AB-731 candidates slip Three recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AB-731 candidates, grounded in the current skills outline. Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Microsoft 365 Copilot are three different entitlements All three share a name and a chat window, which is exactly why AB-731 tests the difference between them. Microsoft 365 Copilot uses organisational context from Microsoft Graph broadly, while Copilot Chat is web-grounded by default. Copilot Chat can still use organisational content that a user explicitly provides or accesses through an agent, so check the scenario's licence and grounding path rather than ruling it out automatically. Generative AI and classical machine learning solve different problems AB-731 expects you to place a described capability on the right side of the ML/AI line before you evaluate it. The exam is testing whether you know a model predicting a numeric outcome is discriminative, not generative. Check what the model actually produces before judging its cost or risk profile. Build, buy, and extend are three different commitments, not synonyms for "use AI" AB-731 stems hide a licensing or engineering-effort constraint inside the wording of a proposal. A described agent has to be sorted into build, buy, or extend before any recommendation makes sense. Match declarative agents to extend, a custom Foundry engine to build, and an existing licence to buy. 4-week study plan Suggested AB-731 study plan Work through AI business value, Microsoft services and adoption decisions. AB-900 is the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent Administration Fundamentals credential — the entry-level exam for IT admins who deploy, govern, and support Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot agents in an enterprise. AB-900 is practical and admin-centre-focused . It covers: Core Microsoft 365 features and objects across admin centres, identity, and security Data protection and governance through Microsoft Purview — Information Protection, DLP, Insider Risk, DSPM for AI, and Data Lifecycle Management How Copilot accesses data via Microsoft Graph while respecting M365, Purview, and Defender controls Basic admin tasks: assigning Copilot licences, monitoring PAYG billing, approving agents, and tracking agent usage across the M365 and Power Platform admin centres Expect questions that ask which admin centre or which Purview tool fits a stated business need. Microsoft published the AB-900 skills outline on 22 July 2026 . Every question in Azure Mastery's AB-900 bank is mapped to the current outline — including the newer DSPM for AI, Copilot Analytics, and SharePoint oversharing topics. Read the official outline at learn.microsoft.com . Questions Typically 35–50; varies Duration 45 minutes (65 min seat) Pass score 700 / 1000 Cost USD $99 (≈ £75 UK) Validity Does not expire (Fundamentals) Format Online or test centre Skills measured · 22 July 2026 AB-900 exam objectives Three domains, weighted by Microsoft's 22 July 2026 release outline. Every domain below lists Microsoft's own skill groups verbatim from the official skills outline , and Azure Mastery tags each question to its assessed domain so you can see which topics need more practice. AI & agent skill map Identify the core features and objects of Microsoft 365 services Published weight 30–35% 113 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Core topics Identify the core objects of Microsoft 365 services Understand the Microsoft 365 security principles Identify the core security features of Microsoft 365 services This domain tests naming the right admin centre — Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, or M365 — for a described object or task. Candidates who've only used one or two admin centres regularly under-prepare for questions about the others. Walk through each admin centre once, matching a handful of objects to the console that actually manages them. Understand data protection and governance tasks for Microsoft 365 and Copilot Published weight 35–40% 127 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Protect topics Understand Microsoft Purview Understand data security implications of Copilot Identify data protection and governance risks for Microsoft 365 and Copilot Identify and monitor oversharing in SharePoint in Microsoft 365 Which Purview surface fits a scenario, from Information Protection through to DSPM for AI, is what this domain actually checks. Older DLP and labelling features often get more study time than newer surfaces like DSPM for AI and oversharing reports. Give DSPM for AI and SharePoint oversharing detection the same attention as classic DLP; this domain weighs heaviest. Perform basic administrative tasks for Copilot and agents Published weight 25–30% 83 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Admin topics Understand features and capabilities of Copilot and agents Perform basic administrative tasks for Copilot Perform basic administrative tasks for agents Licensing, PAYG billing, agent approval, and monitoring usage across two admin centres make up this domain's operational core. Agent administration gets confused with agent building, which is separate Copilot Studio maker work outside this exam. Separate configuring who can use an agent from designing how it responds; only the former is tested here. Common traps Where AB-900 candidates slip Five recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AB-900 candidates, grounded in the current skills outline. Know the primary admin surface for each Microsoft 365 workload Candidates treat the admin centres as interchangeable consoles rather than each owning a distinct set of objects. Object-to-centre mapping is the graded skill, ahead of simply recognising each console by name. Match the object named in the scenario to the primary admin surface for that workload, while remembering that some settings are visible in more than one portal. A Copilot licence and pay-as-you-go billing solve different usage patterns Both are ways to pay for Copilot, so candidates assume the exam only cares that a valid billing method was picked. Usage pattern is the variable under test, since both options technically switch Copilot on for the user. Check whether the scenario describes steady or occasional usage before choosing between a licence and pay-as-you-go billing. DSPM for AI is scoped to AI tools, not general data loss Standard DLP and DSPM for AI both stop sensitive content leaking, so candidates default to the more familiar DLP answer. AB-900 checks whether you route a prompt-or-grounding-data leak to DSPM for AI instead of standard DLP. Pick DSPM for AI whenever the scenario describes a risk coming specifically from a Copilot or agent response. Sensitivity labels protect content; oversharing reports find it after the fact Both sit inside Microsoft Purview, so candidates reach for labelling whenever a question mentions who can access a file. Telling protection from detection apart is the graded skill, since only one tool shows who has access right now. Pick an oversharing report, not a sensitivity label, for any question about auditing who currently has access to a site. Administering an agent is not the same task as building one AB-900 tests who can use, publish, or monitor an agent, never how the agent's own conversation logic works. The admin's job, approving and monitoring an agent, is what's graded here, never the maker's conversation design. Rule out any answer describing conversation design; that work belongs to a separate Copilot Studio certification, not this exam. 3-week study plan Suggested AB-900 study plan Build a Microsoft 365 foundation, then explore data protection and Copilot administration. Allow time for practice and review within this three-week route. Microsoft 365 foundations Review admin-centre settings, Exchange, SharePoint and Teams objects. Compare Zero Trust, authentication and authorisation concepts. Explore Entra access controls, identity troubleshooting and Defender XDR. Data protection and governance Review Purview labels, DLP, retention, insider risk and communication compliance. Explore compliance, investigation and DSPM for AI tools. Trace Copilot data access and address SharePoint oversharing. Copilot, agents and review Compare Copilot and agent capabilities, licensing and usage monitoring. Review agent access, creation, approval and administration. Use Focus Weak Spots, then complete and review two 45-minute simulator sessions.

Implement text analysis solutions Published weight 10–15% 74 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Text topics Apply language model text analysis Implement speech solutions Covers two separate skill sets, language-model text analysis and speech, that candidates lump together as one "language services" bucket. Struggling to name the exact Foundry tool or SDK call a stated text or audio requirement needs is the common miss. Match the scenario's exact requirement — structured JSON, sentiment, or a custom speech model — to its specific Foundry call. Implement information extraction solutions Published weight 10–15% 64 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Extraction topics Build retrieval and grounding pipelines Extract content from documents Where retrieval and document intelligence meet: choosing semantic, hybrid, or vector search for a described grounding scenario. Candidates treat OCR as the deliverable, but it's only a step toward structured or Markdown output for a RAG pipeline. Practise configuring enrichment skills for text, image, and layout before assuming Content Understanding needs no setup. Common traps Where AI-103 candidates slip Five recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AI-103 candidates, grounded in the current skills outline. Right-sizing the model, not maximising it Candidates default to the largest multimodal model offered, when the scenario's latency, cost, and context needs point to a smaller one. Latency, cost, and context length are the three levers Microsoft actually tests — raw capability rarely decides the answer. Treat every "which model" question as a sizing problem first: check latency, cost, and context before capability. RAG is not fine-tuning Candidates reach for RAG when a scenario actually needs model customisation through fine-tuning, or the reverse. RAG grounds answers in your own content at query time; fine-tuning changes the model's weights permanently instead. Read for "answer from our current documents" — that phrase means retrieval, never fine-tuning. One agent with tools vs. orchestrated agents A single agent calling several tools and an orchestrator delegating to separate agents solve different shapes of problem entirely. Scope is the tell: one agent's tools share its memory, while an orchestrator hands each specialised agent its own context. Check whether the scenario needs one agent's shared memory and scope, or separate agents each with their own. Filters, evaluators, and governance aren't the same control Content filters, evaluators, and governance controls all sound like "safety", but each operates at a different point in the pipeline. Runtime filtering blocks content as it flows, evaluation scores it afterwards, and governance sets the rules before either runs. Ask when the control acts — before, during, or after the agent runs — to sort it into the right category. Content Understanding is a full extraction pipeline Candidates treat Content Understanding as simple OCR, missing the structured output and multimodal analysis the exam actually tests. Structured JSON or Markdown output, multimodal analysis, and a direct connection into a RAG pipeline all sit inside Content Understanding. Look for what happens after extraction: structured JSON, Markdown, or a handoff into the next pipeline stage. 6-week study plan Suggested AI-103 study plan Build from Foundry foundations to agents, multimodal apps and information extraction. Follow this six-week route, with focused review and timed practice at the end. Plan and manage AI Review Foundry services, models and deployment choices. Plan CI/CD, monitoring and cost management. Apply security and responsible AI considerations. Generative AI and agents Build RAG solutions with Foundry SDKs. Explore tools, memory and multi-agent orchestration. Review safeguards, evaluation and tracing. Computer vision Explore image and video generation and editing. Review multimodal understanding and Content Understanding. Consider accessibility outputs and visual safety. Text and speech Practise extraction, summarisation and sentiment analysis. Explore translation, speech-to-text and text-to-speech. Review audio-reasoning scenarios. Information extraction Combine multimodal ingestion and OCR. Compare semantic, hybrid and vector search for RAG. Produce structured outputs with Content Understanding. Review and rehearse Use Focus Weak Spots to revisit weaker topics. Complete two timed, 100-minute Exam Simulator sessions. Review mistakes and plan further practice.

AI-200 is the Microsoft Certified: AI Cloud Developer Associate exam — the credential hiring managers expect when posting "AI Cloud Developer", "AI Platform Engineer", or "Vector Database Developer" roles. AI-200 covers building AI-powered cloud solutions on Azure: compute, vector storage, integration pipelines, security and identity for AI workloads, and operational monitoring. AI-200 is hands-on and infrastructure-aware . It covers: Develop AI-powered compute solutions — Azure Functions, Container Apps, AKS for AI workloads Develop for vector-enabled storage and data — Azure Cosmos DB vector search, Azure SQL vector capabilities, Azure AI Search vector indexes Implement AI pipelines and integration — Azure Data Factory, Logic Apps, event-driven patterns Implement security and identity for AI — managed identities, Microsoft Entra, Private Link, content filters Monitor and optimise AI solutions — Application Insights, cost controls, performance tuning Expect scenario questions that combine compute, data, and identity choices. Microsoft updated the AI-200 skills outline on 5 May 2026 , consolidating the previous five-domain structure into four. Every question in Azure Mastery's AI-200 bank is mapped to the current outline — no leftover questions on retired services. Read the official outline at learn.microsoft.com . Questions 40–60 questions, mixed formats Duration 100 minutes (120 min seat) Pass score 700 / 1000 Cost USD $165 (≈ £128 UK) Validity Renew annually (Associate) Format Online or test centre Skills measured · 5 May 2026 AI-200 exam objectives Four domains, with weights set by Microsoft's 5 May 2026 update. Every domain below lists Microsoft's own skill groups verbatim from the official skills outline , so you always know which domain you're being tested on and where your weak spots cluster. AI & agent skill map Develop containerized solutions on Azure Published weight 20–25% 60 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Compute topics Implement container application hosting Implement container-orchestrated solutions Hosts the compute layer AI workloads run on: building images, deploying to App Service, and orchestrating with Container Apps or AKS. A deployment that's merely stood up isn't enough — the exam expects troubleshooting via logs, events, and connectivity too. Practise reading a live deployment's failure signal as closely as the manifest that created it. Develop AI solutions by using Azure data management services Published weight 25–30% 67 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Data topics Develop AI solutions by using Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL Develop AI solutions by using Azure Database for PostgreSQL Integrate Azure Managed Redis in AI solutions The largest domain: Cosmos DB indexing and vectors, PostgreSQL pgvector tuning, and Managed Redis vector search. Candidates treat Cosmos DB, PostgreSQL, and Redis as interchangeable vector databases, missing each one's own tuning knobs. Match the named service in the scenario to its specific configuration surface, not a generic vector-store answer. Connect to and consume Azure services Published weight 20–25% 60 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Integration topics Develop event- and message-based AI solutions Develop and implement Azure Functions Covers choosing Service Bus or Event Grid for a reliability or fan-out need, plus building serverless Azure Functions. Each messaging service gets defined correctly on its own, yet picking the one a described reliability need actually calls for trips people up. Practise choosing between queued and event-driven patterns for a described AI workload — knowing the definitions alone isn't enough. Secure, monitor, and troubleshoot Azure solutions Published weight 20–25% 53 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Operations topics Implement secure Azure solutions Monitor and troubleshoot Azure solutions Splits between security and observability: Key Vault vs App Configuration, and OpenTelemetry tracing vs KQL log queries. Candidates underestimate this domain since it feels less AI-specific, but it carries equal published weight. Given a symptom, practise naming the exact telemetry source or query that surfaces its cause. Common traps Where AI-200 candidates slip Five recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AI-200 candidates, grounded in the current skills outline. Studying the old five-domain outline Candidates study an outdated five-domain outline and underweight how much Container Apps and data services now carry. Container Apps and data services carry more combined weight under the current four-domain structure than under the retired one. Check your study source's date before trusting its domain breakdown — Foundry and AI Search are supporting context now, not headings. Treating every vector store the same way Candidates apply generic "vector database" knowledge instead of a named service's own configuration surface. Cosmos DB, PostgreSQL, and Managed Redis each tune vector search through a different set of settings entirely. Match the scenario's named service to its own indexing or connection settings before answering. Service Bus vs Event Grid — reliability vs reaction Candidates can't tell a guaranteed-delivery requirement from a many-subscribers reaction requirement. Service Bus supports reliable brokered messaging; ordered FIFO processing requires sessions. Event Grid routes discrete events to one or more subscribers. Pick Service Bus for a specific back-end queue, Event Grid for many subscribers reacting to a change. Key Vault secrets vs App Configuration settings Candidates reach for Key Vault to store ordinary configuration that App Configuration was built to hold. Key Vault protects secrets, keys, and certificates; App Configuration is the intended home for non-secret, centralised settings. Ask whether the described value is confidential before choosing Key Vault over App Configuration. OpenTelemetry traces vs KQL log queries Candidates pick a trace-based answer for an aggregate question, or the reverse. Tracing follows a single request end to end; a KQL query answers aggregate questions across many requests at once. Match "where did this one request fail" to tracing, and "what's the error rate" to a KQL query. 6-week study plan Suggested AI-200 study plan Move from AI compute and vector storage to integration, security and operations. Adjust this six-week route to your Azure development experience. AI compute Compare Functions, Container Apps and AKS GPU pools. Manage container images in ACR. Review autoscaling and cold-start mitigation. Vectors and storage Compare Cosmos DB, Azure SQL and Azure AI Search vector options. Distinguish vector search from hybrid search. Practise embedding generation and chunking. Pipelines and integration Compare Data Factory, Synapse pipelines, Logic Apps and Power Automate. Use event-triggered Azure Functions. Design retry and idempotency patterns. Security and identity Use managed identities, app registrations and Foundry RBAC. Review Private Link, customer-managed keys and Key Vault. Configure content filters. Monitoring and optimisation Trace AI calls with Application Insights and custom telemetry. Monitor tokens, latency and cost. Compare caching, batching and capacity-planning choices. Review and rehearse Use Focus Weak Spots to revisit weaker topics. Complete two timed, 100-minute Exam Simulator sessions. Review mistakes and repeat difficult scenarios.

Implement machine learning model lifecycle and operations Published weight 25–30% 102 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore ML Lifecycle topics Orchestrate model training Implement model registration and versioning Deploy machine learning models for production environments Monitor and maintain machine learning models in production Matching a training, registration, deployment, or monitoring step to what the scenario actually needs done is the core skill. Design and implement a GenAIOps infrastructure Published weight 20–25% 84 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore GenAIOps topics Implement Foundry environments and platform configuration Deploy and manage foundation models for production workloads Implement prompt versioning and management with source control Tests configuring Foundry environments, model deployment, and prompt versioning for a stated production need. Provisioned throughput often gets reached for on a spiky, low-volume workload where a Standard pay-per-token deployment fits better. Match identity, network, and deployment choices to the described security and traffic pattern, not habit. Implement generative AI quality assurance and observability Published weight 10–15% 52 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore QA & Observe topics Configure evaluation and validation for generative AI applications and agents Implement observability for generative AI applications and agents Building an evaluation harness before launch is what separates a strong answer, well before problems reach production. Classic drift monitoring often gets applied to a GenAI system instead of tracking groundedness or relevance decay. Learn which metric, groundedness, relevance, coherence, or fluency, actually measures the described failure. Optimize generative AI systems and model performance Published weight 10–15% 54 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Optimize topics Optimize retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) performance and accuracy Implement advanced fine-tuning and model customization Knowing when tuning retrieval beats fine-tuning the model, or neither beats a better base model, is the core test. Candidates tune an embedding model when a compound query was never fully expressed to the retriever. Prove any RAG or fine-tuning improvement with a relevance metric or A/B test rather than instinct. Common traps Where AI-300 candidates slip Five recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AI-300 candidates, grounded in the current skills outline. Registering an MLflow model captures the artifact; it doesn't mean the model is production-ready. A model sitting in the registry with no traffic hasn't been deployed yet, whatever the registration status suggests. Check for a real-time or batch endpoint and a rollout strategy before assuming registration finished the job. Data drift and prompt drift are caught by different monitoring mechanisms. A GenAIOps workload calls for evaluation-metric decay, not classic drift monitoring, as the signal to watch. Match feature-distribution drift to traditional models and groundedness or relevance decay to generative systems. A better embedding model doesn't fix a query the retriever never saw. A missed compound question is a query-construction problem first, not a scoring problem. Check whether every condition in the question was actually expressed before tuning the embedding model. Provisioned throughput solves capacity and latency, not cost, for a spiky workload. A low-volume, spiky workload with a cost constraint usually calls for a Standard pay-per-token deployment, not PTUs. Match billed-regardless-of-usage PTUs to steady high volume, and pay-per-token to unpredictable traffic. A network restriction can silently block the pipeline it was meant to protect. A missing rule or managed identity is what typically breaks right after a workspace or project gets locked down. Grant the specific pipeline, registry share, or monitoring integration through the boundary you just added. 6-week study plan Suggested AI-300 study plan Work through ML operations, then generative AI operations and optimisation. Compare deployment patterns and feature-flag rollouts. Track token usage and cost. Quality and observability Evaluate groundedness and hallucinations. Review content-safety telemetry and prompt or RAG drift. Use distributed tracing to investigate failures. Performance and cost Compare semantic caches, embedding caches and batching. Choose models and weigh fine-tuning, few-shot prompting and RAG. Plan token budgets and capacity. Review and rehearse Use Focus Weak Spots to revisit weaker topics. Complete two timed, 100-minute Exam Simulator sessions. Review mistakes and revisit the underlying trade-offs.

AI-901 is the current exam for the Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals credential. It replaced AI-900 , which retired on 30 June 2026. AI-901 is intended for people starting to work with AI solutions on Azure, including aspiring junior developers who are beginning to add AI capabilities to applications. The exam mixes concepts with hands-on reading. You need core cloud concepts, Azure resources, common AI capabilities, and responsible AI, plus the confidence to follow Python syntax and code examples that call AI models. You'll also use Microsoft Foundry to deploy models and build single-agent solutions. The English AI-901 exam was updated on 15 April 2026 . AI & agent skill map Identify AI concepts and capabilities Published weight 40–45% 252 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Concepts topics Describe principles of responsible AI Identify AI model components and configurations Identify AI workloads Tests whether you can match a responsible AI principle, a model capability, or a workload to a short scenario. Candidates blur agentic AI with plain generative AI, or mix up two of the six responsible AI principles. Learn each of the six principles by the specific harm it addresses, not as a memorised list. Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry Published weight 55–60% 320 exam-scoped practice questions in the app Explore Implement topics Implement generative AI apps and agents by using Foundry Implement AI solutions for text and speech by using Foundry Implement AI solutions with computer vision and image-generation capabilities by using Foundry Implement AI solutions for information extraction by using Foundry A short Python snippet gets matched to the Foundry feature it calls, and that mapping is the real skill on show. A familiar service name doesn't guarantee you can trace what its SDK call actually does. Practise tracing what a snippet's client call deploys, sends, or extracts before you pick an answer. Common traps Where AI-901 candidates slip Three recurring misconceptions that trip up otherwise well-prepared AI-901 candidates, grounded in the current skills outline. Knowing a service name isn't the same as reading the code Candidates who can name Azure AI Language often can't follow a short SDK snippet that deploys a model and reads its response. Scenario questions expect you to trace what a snippet's SDK call actually deploys or returns. Practise reading short SDK snippets end to end, past the import line and the service name. Responsible AI's six principles aren't interchangeable labels Fairness, transparency, and accountability describe different failure modes, and stems often test whether you know which one applies. The exam is testing whether you can match a described real-world harm to the specific principle it breaches. Learn each principle by its own failure mode, not as a flat list of six similar-sounding words. Generative and agentic AI aren't the same workload A single-agent Foundry solution that plans and calls a tool is agentic even though it also generates text. Telling a text-generating workload apart from one that decides and acts is the actual distinction being scored. Ask whether the system only produces content or also plans and executes multi-step actions on its own. 6-week study plan Suggested AI-901 study plan Build AI foundations, then practise with Foundry models, agents and multimodal tools.
